The AI market just crossed the threshold from experimental budget line to enterprise infrastructure spend.

Gartner's latest forecast projects worldwide AI platforms and models spending will reach $64 billion in 2026 — a 63.4% leap from $39 billion in 2025. GenAI model spending alone is growing at 117%.

For executives, the signal is unmistakable. This is no longer discretionary innovation spend. It is capital allocation at scale, and it is accelerating. The companies capturing disproportionate value will not be those with the largest models — they will be the ones that govern where and how AI operates across business functions. Gartner explicitly names this as the long-term competitive differentiator.

The implication: procurement, compliance, and AI orchestration are becoming C-suite priorities on par with cloud migration five years ago. Organizations without a coherent AI deployment strategy are not just behind — they are building on sand while competitors pour concrete.
